artifacts.summary: Confirms the V2 gate root cause by direct reproduction, verifies (and rejects) the naive fix, and specifies the decoupled git-add/git-commit-pathspec fix plus test shapes and the out-of-scope-deletion decision.

memory_candidates.content:
A bash git wrapper that path-scopes a commit via `git add ` then `git commit -- ` must NOT reuse the same pathspec array for both calls when a pathspec can represent an already-staged deletion (e.g. after `git rm`/`git mv`, where the path is gone from both working tree and index). `git add ` errors with 'pathspec did not match any files' (exit 128), and since `git add` takes the whole pathspec array in one invocation, this aborts staging for every other path in the same call too -- turning a silent partial-drop into a loud whole-batch failure. Fix: classify each pathspec into (a) normal (exists on disk or in index) -> goes to both the git-add set and the git-commit set, (b) already-staged deletion (absent from disk+index but present at `git cat-file -e HEAD:

`) -> git-commit set ONLY, skip git add entirely since it's already staged, (c) genuinely unmatched -> drop. Verified directly: `git commit -m ... -- ` succeeds even when only was `git add`-ed, because git commit reads from the index, not disk.
